mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact eliminates the structured definition of role-operation pairs. The LeastPrivilege assertion checks that every (Role, OperationKind) pair is defined; without this fact, the permission matrix becomes empty and the assertion fails to constrain anything.

Removing this fact allows tasks to have zero or multiple owners. The OwnershipExclusivity assertion explicitly checks that each task has exactly one owner; without this constraint, tasks can violate the one-owner invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultiOwner { some t: Task, u1, u2: User | u1 != u2 and (u1 = t.owner or u2 = t.owner) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to record an actor with a role that does not match their actual membership role in that team. The AttributionCorrectness assertion checks this consistency; without the fact, actors can be misattributed.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongActorRole { some ae: AuditEntry, tm: TeamMembership | ae.actorUser = tm.user and ae.team = tm.team and ae.actorRole != tm.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks to exist without any audit entry. The AuditCompleteness assertion requires every task to have at least one entry (the creation); without this constraint, orphan tasks violate the invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoAuditEntry { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.task = t }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks and audit entries to exist without an authenticated actor. The AuthRequiredEverywhere assertion verifies that every operation is performed by a user with valid team membership; without the constraint, unauthenticated operations become possible.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthenticatedOp { some ae: AuditEntry | no u: User | u = ae.actorUser }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a user to have multiple memberships (and thus multiple roles) in the same team. The FR_007 assertion explicitly checks that each (user, team) pair maps to at most one membership; without this constraint, multi-role-per-team becomes possible.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultiRolePerTeam { some u: User, t: Team, tm1, tm2: TeamMembership | tm1 != tm2 and tm1.user = u and tm1.team = t and tm2.user = u and tm2.team = t }
